object_types.name: Customer
object_types.definition: A person or entity who places orders; identified by customer ID in the CRM system.

source_references.excerpt: A customer places an order.
Each customer has a unique customer ID in the CRM system.
In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients."

object_types.name: CustomerId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a customer in the CRM system.

source_references.excerpt: Each customer has a unique customer ID in the CRM system.

object_types.name: CustomerName
object_types.definition: The name of a customer, tracked as a text field.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every customer has a name. It's just a text field.

object_types.name: Order
object_types.definition: A purchase order placed by a customer, containing one or more products.

source_references.excerpt: Every order belongs to exactly one customer
Each order has an order number. That's the primary identifier.

object_types.name: OrderNumber
object_types.definition: The primary identifier of an order.

source_references.excerpt: Each order has an order number. That's the primary identifier.

object_types.name: OrderStatus
object_types.definition: The current status of an order.

source_references.excerpt: The possible values are: pending, confirmed, shipped, and delivered. Every order must have a status.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: An item that can be included in orders; identified by SKU.

source_references.excerpt: An order contains one or more products.
By SKU -- a unique stock-keeping unit code.

object_types.name: Sku
object_types.definition: A unique stock-keeping unit code identifying a product.

source_references.excerpt: By SKU -- a unique stock-keeping unit code.

object_types.name: Quantity
object_types.definition: The number of units of a product specified on an order line.

source_references.excerpt: Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity.

ambiguities.description: The billing system term 'client' appears to be the same concept as 'customer' but with a different qualifying condition (only counted once they've paid). Should 'Client' be modeled as a subtype of Customer with a payment-based condition, or is it purely a naming synonym with no semantic difference for this model?

source_references.excerpt: In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether Order.Status changes over time and whether history of status changes should be tracked (e.g., timestamps for when an order moved from pending to confirmed to shipped to delivered), or whether only the current status matters.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, an order has a status. The possible values are: pending, confirmed, shipped, and delivered.

ambiguities.description: The relationship between Order and Product via order lines includes a Quantity, but it's unclear if an order can have multiple separate lines for the same product (e.g., two lines both referencing the same SKU with different quantities), which would affect whether Order+Product is truly unique.

source_references.excerpt: An order contains one or more products. Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity.
